family.description: This domain is found in diverse bacterial signaling proteins. It is called EAL after its conserved residues. The EAL domain is a good candidate for a diguanylate phosphodiesterase function [[cite:PUB00007150]]. The domain contains many conserved acidic residues that could participate in metal binding and might form the phosphodiesterase active site [[cite:PUB00007150]].

causal_graphs.context: His6-tagged protein expressed from pET-26(b+) in E. coli BL21(DE3). Table 1 assays use 100 mM Tris pH 8.0, 23 C, 20 mM KCl and 25 mM MgCl2. HPLC measures initial product formation below 10% substrate conversion; higher mutant enzyme concentrations permit rate measurement. The substrate and Mg2+ are joint assay inputs, not independent sufficient causes.

evidence.explanation: Methods, Results and Table 1 establish purified-protein conversion and kinetic measurement. Reported cAMP/cGMP negative tests constrain substrate scope; Figure 1 is a reaction schematic, not the measured time course.
Maps the paper's locus to the family using matching reference sequences, not an isolated-domain experiment.
evidence.snippet: Pfam family interval: PF00563 at 147-379, inclusive.

edges.mechanism: Purified RocR converts c-di-GMP to the linear dinucleotide under the stated magnesium-containing assay conditions. Product formation is monitored by HPLC and product mass checked by MALDI-MS; no atomic intermediate is represented.
edges.subject: rocr-hydrolysis

evidence.explanation: Table 1 reports WT kcat 0.67 +/- 0.03 per second and E352Q (1.1 +/- 0.1) x 10^-5 per second, a 6.1 x 10^4-fold decrease. Figure 4 was visually inspected with its different vertical scales. Figure 3 tests E352A at different magnesium levels and is not substituted for these rates.
Verifies reference numbering within the PF00563 interval; the paper supplies the mutagenesis and assay evidence.
evidence.snippet: UniProt and InterPro sequences matched exactly; residue 352 is E.

edges.mechanism: The E352Q variant has lower enzyme-normalized turnover than wild type in the same Table 1 assay. This is an observed substitution effect on catalysis, not direct observation of proton transfer by E352.
edges.subject: rocr-e352q

causal_graphs.family_mapping: PAO1 rocR/sadR, locus PA3947, maps to UniProtKB:Q9HX69 and NCBIProtein:AAG07334.1. Reference sequence version 1 has 392 residues, with PF00563 at 147-379 and E at position 352. The separate PROSITE annotation at 140-392 is not the Pfam boundary. The final recombinant tag junctions were not independently verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: The substitution effect is measured directly, but does not uniquely establish a general-base role or exclude subtle structural changes. The 2012 R286W structure could not discriminate one- versus two-metal catalysis. No RocS1 phosphotransfer, biofilm effect or isolated-domain sufficiency is asserted. Other EAL proteins may be catalytically inactive; this graph covers one tested member.

record.description: This domain is found in diverse bacterial signaling proteins. It is called EAL after its conserved residues. The EAL domain is a good candidate for a diguanylate phosphodiesterase function [[cite:PUB00007150]]. The domain contains many conserved acidic residues that could participate in metal binding and might form the phosphodiesterase active site [[cite:PUB00007150]].

evidence.explanation: Table 1 and Figures 3-4 were inspected. Mutant kinetics support a turnover defect; pH dependence and docking motivate but do not directly observe a proton-transfer mechanism.
The later primary study explicitly leaves the one- versus two-metal distinction unresolved in its R286W structure and presents phosphorylation-dependent modulation as putative.

discussions.notes: The 2012 interpretation is retained in evidence/PF00563/chen-2012-rocr-limits.txt. Other mutations, experimental contexts and later literature have not received a complete family review. Status remains IN_PROGRESS.
discussions.prompt: Resolve construct details, competing catalytic models and additional EAL member contexts before expanding this graph.
discussions.rationale: Two direct assay-level edges do not determine atomistic catalysis, phosphorylation-dependent activation or a downstream cellular phenotype. Family membership is not evidence of catalytic competence for every EAL protein.
